Answer: A
Reason: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (Hamman's syndrome) due to alveolar rupture typically presents with mediastinal air and subcutaneous emphysema but lacks the pleural effusion, hydropneumothorax, or severe lung opacification characteristic of esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome). The absence of adjacent lung opacification or effusion on the chest X-ray strongly favors an alveolar etiology over an esophageal leak.
